skill.name: codex-pet
skill.description: Codex Pet generator on RunComfy. Build a Codex-compatible Codex Pet spritesheet.webp + pet.json from a single reference image, drop it into `${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/pets/<name>/` and Codex picks it up as a custom Codex Pet next to the 8 built-ins. This skill produces the exact Codex Pet atlas Codex expects (1536x1872 PNG/WebP, 8 cols x 9 rows, 192x208 cells, 9 animation states — idle, running-right, running-left, waving, jumping, failed, waiting, running, review). Calls OpenAI GPT Image 2 edit ONCE via the local RunComfy CLI as `runcomfy run openai/gpt-image-2/edit` to produce a canonical Codex Pet pose, then assembles all 9 animation rows programmatically with ImageMagick micro-transforms — no Codex Pro, no `$imagegen`, no OPENAI_API_KEY required, only RUNCOMFY_TOKEN. Triggers on "codex pet", "create codex pet", "make codex pet", "hatch codex pet", "/hatch image", "desktop pet codex", "codex pets", "spritesheet.webp", or any explicit ask to build a custom pet for OpenAI Codex.

security_audit.summary: All 83 static alerts are false positives involving Markdown, ordinary commands, documentation links, configuration paths, or authentication terminology. One semantic risk remains: customizable names lack path validation before artifact creation and installation. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection or credential theft; the documented workflow sends the source image to RunComfy.

remediation.issue: Configurable names are used in working and installation paths without directory confinement.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only simple name characters, reject path separators and parent segments, verify resolved destinations remain inside intended roots, and confirm before overwriting files.

semantic_findings.description: PET_NAME is appended to working and installation paths without rejecting separators or parent segments. A crafted name can redirect artifact writes outside intended roots and overwrite matching filenames.

content.user_title: Create Custom Codex Pets From Reference Images
content.value_statement: Creating a custom Codex pet requires a correctly sized sprite atlas and manifest. This skill combines RunComfy image generation with ImageMagick assembly and local installation.
actual_capabilities: Generate one canonical sprite from a publicly accessible reference image through the RunComfy GPT Image 2 edit endpoint.
Remove a solid chroma-key background and normalize the sprite into a transparent 192x208 cell.
Build nine animation rows using shifts, rotations, blink overlays, mirroring, and transparent trailing cells.
Assemble a 1536x1872 sprite atlas and convert the PNG output to WebP.
Write pet.json and copy it with spritesheet.webp into the configured Codex custom asset directory.
Adjust movement offsets and rotation values by editing the documented animation recipes.
limitations: Requires RunComfy authentication, network access, ImageMagick, and a publicly fetchable HTTPS source image; the source is processed by RunComfy.
Animation derives from one pose and small image transforms, not distinct model-generated action frames.
Background removal can erase similar subject colors, and image generation can alter identifying details.
The supplied shell examples do not validate custom names or safely encode arbitrary metadata; review names and descriptions before execution.

best_practices: Use an image you may share with RunComfy, and confirm authentication and expected charges before the model call.
Use simple names without path separators, verify destination containment, and approve replacement of existing assets.
Inspect transparency, atlas dimensions, frame counts, and identifying details before installing the generated files.
anti_patterns: Using sensitive source images or placing authentication tokens in prompts, shared commands, or published output.
Passing unvalidated path-like names or unescaped free-form metadata directly into the supplied shell examples.
Expecting dramatic action sequences from one pose or changing the fixed atlas layout without checking compatibility.

faq.question: Which tools are required?
faq.answer: The workflow uses the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, ImageMagick, and a shell supporting the documented Bash syntax.

faq.question: Does this workflow require an OpenAI API key?
faq.answer: The documented workflow authenticates through RunComfy using login or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN. It does not require OPENAI_API_KEY.

faq.question: Does the source image leave my machine?
faq.answer: Yes. RunComfy fetches the supplied image URL for remote processing. Use only images you are permitted to share.

faq.question: What files does the workflow produce?
faq.answer: The final package contains pet.json and spritesheet.webp. Intermediate files include the canonical image, normalized cell, row strips, and PNG atlas.

faq.question: How are the animation frames created?
faq.answer: One generated pose supplies every row. ImageMagick creates subtle differences through shifting, rotation, blink overlays, and mirroring.

faq.question: Where are the final files installed?
faq.answer: They go under the pets directory inside CODEX_HOME, or the default .codex directory in your home folder. Validate names before installation.
